items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1958-05-24
items.q: Walter Prustin, George Boyd, Chester's artist, Lil' Chinese, and myself. You see, them times, no saxophone.

ctx.x: I mean, look at his family. That's right.
Well, plan it. I had a nice boy in me, and George Boyd, he made it good.
Did I tell you about reading that book by William Faulkner, the famous prize-winning novelist?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: A fellow like, George Boyd, right... George Boyd. Then he had a, what you call him, a trill or three... my boy I had to have me play much clarinet as hot clarinet than anybody I want to hear, George Boyd.

ctx.x: First. And then Louis, and you and guys like you picked it up. Yeah. Well, who's the first trumpet player you ever heard do that?

Well, I'd say, I wouldn't say Louis, I don't know, I swear, I don't know, just, they all started doing it, that's all I see. A fellow like, George Boyd, right, a piece they call number one, where he'd take a chord, the band stopped, and then the trumpet ticket, and the band stopped behind him, you see, make stop time behind him. So, that was just going like that, that's all I can see. Yeah.
What was number one, how did that go?
